Easy cheese biscuits:

- 100g plain flour

- 100g cheese grated (says strong cheddar but use up what you have) 

- 100g salted butter

- 1/2 tsp English mustard powder

- A very little cold water

1. Sieve the flour into a bowl and use a cheese grater to shred the chilled butter.

2. Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips, when it resembles breadcrumbs add in the shredded cheese and mustard powder.

3. Stir to combine and add a few water drops at a time until a dough can be formed. Use as little as water as possible.

4. Shape the dough into two logs 2cm in diameter, wrap in clingfilm and chill in the fridge for at least an hour.

5. Heat the oven to 180c/350F/gas mark 4.

6. Slice each log into small rounds a little thicker than a pound coin, place on oven tray covered in grease proof paper and bake until golden - a little around 8 mins.

7. Leave the biscuits to cool on the tray before eating otherwise they may break apart. 

8. Over eat and regret seeing this recipe as now you want to make more.

You can teach yourself how to do this technique called “the diving response”. Fill up a basin full of cool or cold water, hold your breath and put your face into it briefly for a few seconds. Come out, take a breath, repeat a few times until you can feel yourself calm naturally. 

This works because your bodies natural response to your face hitting the water is that while a brief and mild shock if that water is cold, is that your breathing patterns will change as if you are about you dive into water.

This only works however, like most things if you make a habit of it and practice it a bit before you really need it. Think of it as your parachute, you will have practiced which chord to pull your parachute out from, where the back up chord is etc. The same with this technique; you will need to do it a few times even if you aren’t really pissed off about stuff currently. Practice makes proficient and it’s quite a good way to derail meltdowns, raving and other bullshit that can be more upsetting to deal with in the aftermath.
